primary_claim: On the new BELLS benchmark, simply asking a frontier LLM 'is this prompt harmful?' substantially outperforms specialized commercial misuse-supervision systems (e.g. Lakera Guard, LLM Guard, Langkit, Llama Guard, NeMo), which show very limited semantic understanding and generalization (sometimes 0% detection on direct or novel jailbreak encodings like base64); however, frontier LLMs still lack metacognitive coherence, often answering questions they themselves flag as harmful (up to 30% for Claude 3.7 Sonnet, over 50% for Mistral Large).

effect.metric: detection rate / BELLS score: specialized supervisors vs frontier-LLM baseline prompt
effect.value: specialized systems' detection rate drops to 0% for some systems on direct or base64-encoded harmful prompts in categories like CBRN and malware; a 3-model voting ensemble raised the best detection rate from 90% to 94%

contradicts_or_qualifies: Distinguishes this work from the AI control agenda (Greenblatt et al.), which addresses controlling AI systems that fake alignment, whereas BELLS targets detection of user misuse
stated_future_work: More research is needed to assess the tradeoffs of scaffolding-based misuse-detection techniques
Study the robustness of specific subparts of an AI system, such as monitoring systems, much more thoroughly
Obtain third-party access to systems like Anthropic's constitutional classifiers to assess their robustness across diverse misuse scenarios
limitations_stated: The authors do not have access to the monitoring systems of frontier AI companies
Only five specialized supervision systems were evaluated, a limited sample of the broader landscape; findings may not generalize to all specialized solutions, especially proprietary or future ones
All tested Llama models failed to answer the repurposed 'is this harmful' prompt more than 50% of the time, so results for that family were not exploitable
The full dataset is not publicly released, to prevent misuse of harmful prompts and gaming of the benchmark
Higher detection accuracy does not imply robustness: on the BET leaderboard, 100% of tested models displayed harmful responses on every behavior tested
quote: Simply asking generalist LLMs if the user's question is "harmful or not" largely outperforms these supervisors from the market according to our BELLS score.
